newsitem.title: USA: Music fair regrets Miami ban on Cuban musicians.
newsitem.headline: Music fair regrets Miami ban on Cuban musicians.

text.p: A major music industry trade fair said on Thursday it regretted that Miami officials had banned Cuban artists and representives from attending its Latin American showcase next month.

Dozens of acts ranging from salsa to reggae are lined up to play during the four-day MIDEM Latin American and Caribbean Music Market, a gathering of artists, agents, publishers and other industry figures.
But officials in Miami, which has a vocal Cuban exile community opposed to President Fidel Castro's communist government, have decreed no representatives from Cuba may attend.

"As organisers of MIDEM we find ourselves in a most regrettable position when we are not able to welcome all the professionals -- musicians, authors and artists -- who would like to be present," MIDEN said in a statement from Paris.
"We certainly hope that the cultural side of this situation, with particular emphasis on music, will change in the near future."
It said MIDEM had never been a political platform and was in favour of cultural exchanges.

"The poltical status quo between the United States and Cuba and the laws which govern it as well as the especially sensitive situation in Florida and particularly the city of Miami vis-a-vis this dilemma have obliged us to respect the strict rules put in place by the Greater Miami Convention and Visitors Bureau," it said.

The island's musicians are widely seen as some of the most dynamic and creative in the region and Cuban groups such as Los Van Van have performed to acclaim eleswhere in the United States. Cuban-U.S. cultural exchanges are permitted under national law despite a U.S. embargo on the island.

But Miami officials said no Cubans would be permitted to attend MIDEM. Other Cuban artists or other performers deemed sympathetic to Castro who have tried to play in Miami have met a hostile and sometimes violent reaction from exile groups.
MIDEM artistic director Bernard Batzen said earlier that MIDEM did not wish to hurt the feelings of the Cuban exile community even though he considered Cuban musicians highly talented.

French-based MIDEM (International Record, Music Publishing and Video Music Market) also holds annual fairs in Cannes and Hong Kong. The September 11 event in Miami will be its first dedicated to Latin and Caribbean music.
